stemMd: The passage argues that animal counts

options.label: A
options.textMd: measure only equipment quality and never ecology.

options.label: B
options.textMd: must be interpreted through the conditions and behavior affecting detection.

options.label: C
options.textMd: become exact population totals when cameras replace observers.

options.label: D
options.textMd: are useless unless every animal is individually identified.

options.label: E
options.textMd: should always be multiplied by one fixed correction factor.

explanationMd: The passage connects measurement to animal behavior and environmental conditions. Its conclusion differentiates valid uses of a consistent count from stronger claims about absolute abundance across habitats.

distractorRationale.a: The author says detectability is partly biological.
distractorRationale.c: The camera comparison reveals continuing detection variation.
distractorRationale.d: The passage retains a role for consistent monitoring.
distractorRationale.e: The changing relationship rules out that simple solution.
